answer: Bonded staking forces each agent to lock slashable cryptocurrency into a protocol kernel before participating in market coordination. When Byzantine actions or identity duplications echo through peer gossip, the deposit is permanently slashed. An attacker must commit scarce liquid capital per identity, facing an unyielding economic reef of linear escrow costs. However, locking collateral imposes high capital inefficiency and economically disenfranchises resource-constrained agents.
